sentences.zh: 正好是我们首次将《隐藏的大脑》带给世界十周年的日子。

sentences.en: Welcome to the first episode of the Hidden Brain podcaSt. I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《隐藏的大脑》播客的第一期节目。我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: A lot has changed since we started this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 自从我们创办这个播客以来，发生了很多变化。

sentences.en: But for us, one thing remains steadfaSt.
sentences.zh: 但对我们而言，有一件事始终坚定不移。

sentences.en: Week in and week out, we love making this show for you.
sentences.zh: 周复一周，我们都热爱为你制作这个节目。

sentences.en: It's been our calling.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的天职。

sentences.en: So today, we mark this anniversary with an episode about just that,
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我们通过一期专门探讨这个主题的节目来庆祝这个周年纪念，

sentences.en: callings, and how finding one can change our lives.
sentences.zh: 也就是天职，以及找到天职如何改变我们的生活。

sentences.zh: 我将于10月11日去巴尔的摩，10月12日去华盛顿特区，

sentences.zh: （接上一句）

sentences.zh: 以及11月22日去洛杉矶。

sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息并购票，请访问 hiddenbrain.org slash tour。

sentences.zh: 希望能在那儿见到你，接下来是今天的节目。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: In 2005, an intense man with a receding hairline and glasses
sentences.zh: 2005年，在加利福尼亚州帕洛阿尔托，一位发际线后移、戴着眼镜、神情坚毅的男子

sentences.en: stood before thousands of young graduates in Palo Alto, California.
sentences.zh: 站在成千上万名年轻毕业生面前。

sentences.en: He wore dark robes with a hood of cardinal red.
sentences.zh: 他身穿黑色长袍，披着象征红衣主教红的风帽。

sentences.en: Truth be told, he joked, I never graduated from college,
sentences.zh: 老实说，他开玩笑说，我从未上过大学，

sentences.en: and this is the closest I've ever gotten to a college graduation.
sentences.zh: 而这是我离大学毕业最近的一次。

sentences.en: The speech that Steve Jobs gave at Stanford University's commencement that year
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·乔布斯那年在斯坦福大学毕业典礼上的演讲

sentences.en: didn't just transfix his audience.
sentences.zh: 不仅迷住了现场的听众。

sentences.en: It would transfix countless other audiences in the years to come.
sentences.zh: 在未来的岁月里，它还将迷住无数其他听众。

sentences.en: His central message was simple.
sentences.zh: 他的核心信息很简单。

sentences.en: As he put it, your time is limited.
sentences.zh: 正如他所说，你的时间是有限的。

sentences.en: Don't waste it living someone else's life.
sentences.zh: 不要浪费时间去过别人的生活。

sentences.en: I'm convinced that the only thing that kept me going was that I loved what I did.
sentences.zh: 我坚信，让我坚持下去的唯一原因，就是我热爱我所做的事。

sentences.en: You've got to find what you love,
sentences.zh: 你必须找到你所爱的东西，

sentences.en: and that is as true for work as it is for your lovers.
sentences.zh: 这对于工作来说和对于你的爱人来说同样真实。

sentences.en: Finding a vocation, the inventor and entrepreneur said,
sentences.zh: 这位发明家兼企业家说，寻找职业，

sentences.en: was no less important than finding a soulmate.
sentences.zh: 与寻找灵魂伴侣同样重要。

sentences.en: As with all matters of the heart, you'll know when you find it.
sentences.zh: 正如所有与心灵相关的事情一样，当你找到它时，你自然会知道。

sentences.en: And like any great relationship, it just gets better and better as the years roll on.
sentences.zh: 就像任何伟大的恋情一样，随着岁月的流逝，它会变得越来越好。

sentences.en: And what if you hadn't found something you loved?
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有找到你所爱的东西呢？

sentences.en: What if the work you did paid the bills, but didn't complete you?
sentences.zh: 如果你做的工作只是为了付清账单，却不能让你感到完整呢？

sentences.en: The iconoclastic leader of Apple Inc.
sentences.zh: 苹果公司的这位标志性领袖

sentences.en: had very definite advice for the recent graduates.
sentences.zh: 对这些年轻毕业生有着非常明确的建议。

sentences.en: Your work is going to fill a large part of your life,
sentences.zh: 你的工作将占据你生活很大的一部分，

sentences.en: and the only way to be truly satisfied is to do what you believe is great work.
sentences.zh: 而获得真正满足感的唯一方法，就是去做你认为伟大工作的事。

sentences.en: And the only way to do great work is to love what you do.
sentences.zh: 而做好伟大工作的唯一方法，就是热爱你所做的事。

sentences.en: If you haven't found it yet, keep looking and don't settle.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有找到，继续寻找，不要妥协。

sentences.en: The idea of being driven by a calling goes back centuries.
sentences.zh: 受天职驱使的理念可以追溯到几个世纪前。

sentences.en: It was the language used to describe religious people
sentences.zh: 这是用来描述那些宗教人士的语言，

sentences.en: who were called to the priesthood, to a life of service and prayer.
sentences.zh: 他们被召唤进入神职，过着奉献和祈祷的生活。

sentences.en: You were called, in effect, by God.
sentences.zh: 实际上，你是受到上帝的召唤。

sentences.en: Today, millions of people in secular professions yearn to be similarly galvanized by their work.
sentences.zh: 今天，数以百万计从事世俗职业的人渴望同样被他们的工作所激励。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, the immense power and the downsides of pursuing a calling.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，我们将探讨追求天职的巨大力量与弊端。

sentences.en: Have you ever looked up from your work in the middle of the day and asked yourself,
sentences.zh: 你是否曾在白天的某个时刻从工作中抬起头来问自己，

sentences.en: is this all there is?
sentences.zh: 难道生活仅此而已吗？

sentences.en: Am I really doing what I was meant to do?
sentences.zh: 我做的是我命中注定要做的事吗？

sentences.en: What are the thoughts and images that go through your mind at times like this?
sentences.zh: 在这样的时刻，你脑海中闪过的是什么想法和画面？

sentences.en: Who do you compare yourself to?
sentences.zh: 你把自己和谁作比较？

sentences.en: What do you wish you were doing instead?
sentences.zh: 你希望自己当时在做什么？

sentences.en: At Babson College, Jennifer Tosti-Karas studies how we find meaning in work
sentences.zh: 在巴布森学院，詹妮弗·托斯蒂-卡拉斯研究我们如何在工作中寻找意义，

sentences.en: and ways we can derive more satisfaction and purpose in our professional lives.
sentences.zh: 以及在职业生涯中获得更多满足感和目标感的方法。

sentences.en: Jennifer Tosti-Karas, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗·托斯蒂-卡拉斯，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，香卡。

sentences.en: Jen, I want to start with the story of a stockbroker in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 珍，我想从一个19世纪股票经纪人的故事开始。

sentences.en: What do we know about Paul Gauguin's life as a middle-class breadwinner in 19th century Paris?
sentences.zh: 关于保罗·高更在19世纪巴黎作为中产阶级顶梁柱的生活，我们了解多少？

sentences.en: Yeah, so before he was the celebrated, world-renowned artist that we know today,
sentences.zh: 是的，在他成为我们今天所知的这位举世闻名的著名艺术家之前，

sentences.en: Paul Gauguin was a work-a-day stiff.
sentences.zh: 保罗·高更只是一个普通的上班族。

sentences.en: He was a very reluctant stock trader.
sentences.zh: 他是一个极其不情愿的股票交易员。

sentences.en: He hated this job, which required him to sort of, you know, dress up, put in long hours in the office.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌这份工作，这需要他某种程度上，你知道的，盛装打扮，在办公室里工作很长时间。

sentences.en: And he had this sort of, let's call it a side pursuit, maybe not quite a side hustle,
sentences.zh: 他有这样一种追求，我们称之为副业吧，或许算不上严格意义上的副业，

sentences.en: but he certainly had this interest outside of work, which was art, and both making art and collecting art.
sentences.zh: 但他确实有工作之外的兴趣，那就是艺术，包括创作艺术和收藏艺术。

sentences.en: Perhaps you know someone like this, whose days are filled with work they deteSt.
sentences.zh: 也许你认识这样的人，他们的日子里充满了他们痛恨的工作。

sentences.en: Perhaps you feel this way yourself and wonder how your life could have turned out differently.
sentences.zh: 也许你也有这种感觉，并想知道如果人生重来，会有什么不同。

sentences.en: In 1882, the stock market crashed and Paul Gauguin lost his day job.
sentences.zh: 1882年，股市崩盘，保罗·高更失去了他的正职工作。

sentences.en: He started to look for work that would pay the bills.
sentences.zh: 他开始寻找能付清账单的工作。

sentences.en: He was in a situation that so many people do find themselves,
sentences.zh: 他陷入了许多人都会发现自己所在的处境中，

sentences.en: where essentially to try to make a living, to try to support your family,
sentences.zh: 基本上为了谋生，为了养家糊口，

sentences.en: I mean truly in a subsistence way, he was casting about for any job he could find.
sentences.zh: 我是说真正意义上的勉强糊口，他到处寻找能找到的任何工作。

sentences.en: Even as he was struggling to make ends meet, Paul Gauguin kept returning to his passion.
sentences.zh: 尽管保罗·高更一直在为生计苦苦挣扎，但他始终回归于他的热情。

sentences.en: Art was his refuge, his calling.
sentences.zh: 艺术是他的避难所，是他的天职。

sentences.en: Would he ever be happy if he kept ignoring it?
sentences.zh: 如果他一直忽视它，他会快乐吗？

sentences.en: This is part of the power of this story, in the sense of,
sentences.zh: 这也是这个故事力量的一部分，从某种意义上说，

sentences.en: what if then, to escape this drudgery, I made a radical break?
sentences.zh: 如果为了逃避这种日复一日的枯燥工作，我做出彻底的决裂会怎样？

sentences.en: Sort of, if I'm not fulfilled here, might I be better fulfilled or more fulfilled elsewhere?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果我在这里没有得到满足，我在别处会不会得到更好或更多的满足？

sentences.en: And in a way, that's a lot closer to my passions.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这更贴近我的热情。

sentences.en: Paul Gauguin took a move that a lot of us wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 保罗·高更采取了许多人不敢采取的行动。

sentences.en: So after trying various attempts to move in new cities, he left everything, truly chucked it all,
sentences.zh: 所以在尝试了搬到不同城市未果后，他抛弃了一切，真正彻底放弃了这一切，

sentences.en: upended his life, and moved to Tahiti and pursued his art full-time.
sentences.zh: 颠覆了自己的生活，搬到了大溪地，全职追求他的艺术。

sentences.en: Paul Gauguin's life after he moved to Tahiti has been the subject of a great deal of scrutiny
sentences.zh: 保罗·高更搬到大溪地后的生活一直是现代传记作家和艺术史学家

sentences.en: among modern biographers and art historians.
sentences.zh: 大量仔细研究的主题。

sentences.en: In Tahiti, then a French colony, he lived for years with a 13-year-old girl.
sentences.zh: 在大溪地（当时是法国殖民地），他和一个13岁的女孩一起生活了多年。

sentences.en: He impregnated a 14-year-old.
sentences.zh: 他让一个14岁的女孩怀孕了。

sentences.en: Such behavior would be both illegal and disturbing to people in many parts of the world today.
sentences.zh: 这种行为在当今世界的许多地方既不合法又令人不安。

sentences.en: But in the 19th century, the legal age for sexual consent in France and French colonies was 13.
sentences.zh: 但在19世纪，法国及法国殖民地的法定性同意年龄是13岁。

sentences.en: When Paul Gauguin died in 1903, he was still relatively unknown.
sentences.zh: 1903年保罗·高更去世时，他仍然默默无闻。

sentences.en: Jennifer says that changed after his death.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗说这种情况在他死后发生了变化。

sentences.en: So we know now posthumously, he was extremely successful.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在知道，在他死后，他取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: And again, he's one of those names that, if you can name a few painters, famous painters, he's likely one of them.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，他是那种如果你能说出几个画家的名字、著名画家，他很可能就是其中之一的人。

sentences.en: So we remember Paul Gauguin today not for his acumen as a stockbroker or his skill as a sales rep,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们今天纪念保罗·高更，不是因为他作为股票经纪人的敏锐度或作为销售代表的技能，

sentences.en: but for his art.
sentences.zh: 而是因为他的艺术。

sentences.en: And his paintings, of course, hang in the world's preeminent museums today.
sentences.zh: 当然，他的画作今天悬挂在世界最顶尖的博物馆里。

sentences.en: Do you think, at least in depth, he would say that his gamble paid off?
sentences.zh: 你认为，至少从深远影响来看，他会说他的这场豪赌得到了回报吗？

sentences.en: It would be hard not to say that, again, given the level of fame, notoriety, perhaps infamy, but, you know, that he's enjoyed.
sentences.zh: 鉴于他所享有的名气、声誉，也许是恶名，但你知道的，很难不这么说。

sentences.en: So Paul Gauguin was so influential, not only on his peers, so people like Vincent van Gogh,
sentences.zh: 所以保罗·高更极具影响力，不仅对他的同龄人，比如文森特·梵高，

sentences.en: but on, you know, generations of artists to come, not least of which was Pablo Picasso.
sentences.zh: 而且对后来的几代艺术家，其中最著名的就是巴勃罗·毕加索。

sentences.en: So art historians have drawn a direct line from the oceanic iconography and styling.
sentences.zh: 因此，艺术史学家在海洋风格的图像和造型之间画出了一条直接的线索。

sentences.en: You know, it's not completely naturalistic.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这并非完全写实。

sentences.en: It's somewhat abstract representation of form in Gauguin's Tahitian figures and the work of Picasso and Cubism.
sentences.zh: 高更的大溪地人物作品中对形态的表现带有一些抽象色彩，这影响了毕加索和立体主义的作品。

sentences.en: So in terms of his impact on art today as we know it, it's been massive.
sentences.zh: 因此，就他对我们今天所知的艺术的影响而言，它是巨大的。

sentences.en: And therefore, it's very hard to look and say that this gamble didn't pay off.
sentences.zh: 因此，很难看着这一切说这场豪赌没有得到回报。

sentences.en: In fact, absent this huge risk to chuck it all and move to Tahiti,
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果没有冒着抛弃一切并搬到大溪地的巨大风险，

sentences.en: we would not have the art that I love going to the MFA in Boston
sentences.zh: 我们就不会拥有我喜欢去波士顿美术馆（MFA）欣赏的那些艺术品，

sentences.en: and looking at this giant, famous, maybe one of the most iconic Gauguin paintings,
sentences.zh: 也不会看到那幅巨大的、著名的、也许是最具标志性的高更画作之一，

sentences.en: which hangs proudly there.
sentences.zh: 它就骄傲地悬挂在那里。

sentences.en: And we would not have this beautiful art that everyone appreciates and loves to look at.
sentences.zh: 我们也无法拥有每个人都欣赏和喜爱观看的这些美丽的艺术品。

sentences.en: I want to talk about another person who had a giant effect as a result of her work
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈另一个人，她的工作产生了巨大的影响，

sentences.en: and also influenced a number of people who came after her.
sentences.zh: 并且也影响了许多后来者。

sentences.en: This is the scientist Marie Curie.
sentences.zh: 这就是科学家玛丽·居里。

sentences.en: She was a physicist who was famously devoted to her work.
sentences.zh: 她是一位以献身工作而闻名的物理学家。

sentences.en: Talk about the impact she had, Jennifer.
sentences.zh: 聊聊她产生的影响吧，珍。

sentences.en: Her impact today is widely felt in the use of radiology and medicine.
sentences.zh: 今天，她在放射学和医学的应用中产生了广泛的影响。

sentences.en: She's completely changed the way we think about radioactivity,
sentences.zh: 她彻底改变了我们对放射性的看法，

sentences.en: evident in so many domains of modern life.
sentences.zh: 这在现代生活的许多领域都显而易见。

sentences.en: Yet on top of that, perhaps in a way that we wouldn't say Gauguin was,
sentences.zh: 然而除此之外，或许是以一种高更所没有的方式，

sentences.en: Marie Curie was a groundbreaker.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·居里是一位开创者。

sentences.en: So she was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.
sentences.zh: 所以她是第一位获得诺贝尔奖的女性。

sentences.en: She was not only that, the first person to win a Nobel Prize twice and in separate disciplines,
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，她还是第一位两次获得诺贝尔奖且跨越不同学科的人，

sentences.en: so in physics and in chemistry.
sentences.zh: 也就是在物理学和化学领域。

sentences.en: Similarly, her sort of all or nothing, all in commitment to doing the science,
sentences.zh: 同样地，她那种非此即彼、全心投入科学的承诺，

sentences.en: I think really sets it apart.
sentences.zh: 我认为确实让她与众不同。

sentences.en: So this is similarly someone who was somewhat obsessed with her work,
sentences.zh: 所以这也是一个对工作有些着迷的人，

sentences.en: put a great deal into it, and for her, it wasn't about, you know, fame or recognition.
sentences.zh: 投入了大量心血，对她而言，这无关名誉或认可。

sentences.en: She famously gave away her Nobel Prize money to students who needed it,
sentences.zh: 众所周知，她把诺贝尔奖金捐给了需要的学生，

sentences.en: but she, you know, she was a towering figure who we recognize today.
sentences.zh: 但她，你知道的，她是一位我们今天所认可的高耸人物。

sentences.en: And it's also clear, Jen, that looking back, we know that she paid an enormous price
sentences.zh: 而且很明显，珍，回过头来看，我们知道她为自己作为科学家的成功付出了巨大的代价。

sentences.en: for her success as a scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多人认为她是死于对放射性研究的追求。

sentences.en: In fact, many people believe she died as a result of her pursuit of the study of radioactivity.
sentences.zh: （接上一句）

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think that is really the ultimate symbol of us being willing to sacrifice everything for our work
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这确实是我们愿意为工作牺牲一切的终极象征，

sentences.en: is the willingness to potentially die as a result of the work or related to the work that we're doing,
sentences.zh: 那就是愿意因我们正在做的工作或与之相关的工作而潜在地死去，

sentences.en: whether it's directly from the work itself or as a result of not taking care of ourselves
sentences.zh: 无论是直接死于工作本身，还是由于没有照顾好自己，

sentences.en: because we are doing, we are pursuing work that we love.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在做、在追求我们热爱的工作。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So as I was preparing for this interview, Jen, I came by a clip from an American pioneer.
sentences.zh: 所以在准备这次采访时，珍，我偶然看到了一段来自一位美国先驱的音频片段。

sentences.en: She was born in poverty in Mississippi to a single mom,
sentences.zh: 她出生在密西西比州的贫困家庭，由单亲妈妈抚养长大，

sentences.en: but she always felt like she was cut out for great things.
sentences.zh: 但她总觉得自己是块成大事的料。

sentences.en: I want you to listen to this clip from Oprah Winfrey.
sentences.zh: 我想让你听听这段奥普拉·温弗瑞的讲话。

sentences.en: Sometimes the calling is right in your own neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 有时，天职就在你自己的社区里。

sentences.en: Sometimes the calling is something that was just a whisper to you.
sentences.zh: 有时，天职只是对你的一声轻声呢喃。

sentences.en: And when you begin to honor that whisper and to follow that, you end up being the best that you could be.
sentences.zh: 当你开始尊重那种呢喃并去追随它时，你最终会成为最好的自己。

sentences.en: Now, Oprah, of course, went on to become a billionaire.
sentences.zh: 当然，奥普拉后来成了一名亿万富翁。

sentences.en: You know, people have begged her to run for president.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，大家曾懇求她競選總統。

sentences.en: So we've looked at a painter in the 19th century, a scientist in the 20th century,
sentences.zh: 所以我們探討了19世紀的畫家、20世紀的科學家，

sentences.en: and a television star in the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 以及21世紀的電視明星。

sentences.en: Do you hear common threads in these stories, Jen?
sentences.zh: 珍，你在這些故事中聽到了什麼共同的主線嗎？

sentences.en: So absolutely.
sentences.zh: 確實如此。

sentences.en: I think the common thread here is this notion that work can be a calling.
sentences.zh: 我認為這裡的共同主線是這種觀念：工作可以是一種天職。

sentences.en: It can be more than just a paycheck.
sentences.zh: 它不僅僅是一份薪水。

sentences.en: It can be a source of personal fulfillment, of doing great things in the world.
sentences.zh: 它還可以是個人成就感的來源，是為世界創造偉大成就的途徑。

sentences.en: And as we talked about, a really deep sense of immersing yourself in the doing of the work.
sentences.zh: 正如我們所談到的，這是一種深深投入於工作過程中的感覺。

sentences.en: It does show the power, I believe, of viewing one's work as more than, if you will, just a job,
sentences.zh: 我相信，這確實展現了將工作視為不僅僅是「工作」的力量，如果你願意這麼說的話，

sentences.en: but as a real possibility to contribute both to yourself and to the world at large.
sentences.zh: 而是將其視為對自己和整個世界做出貢獻的真正契機。

sentences.en: When we come back, the psychology of vocations and how we can all find greater meaning in our work.
sentences.zh: 廣告過後，我們將探討職業的心理學，以及我們如何才能在工作中找到更深層的意義。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收聽的是《隱形大腦》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·維丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 這是《隱形大腦》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·維丹塔姆。

sentences.en: When Steve Jobs spoke at Stanford's commencement in 2005, he told the story of why he dropped out of college.
sentences.zh: 當史蒂夫·賈伯斯在2005年史丹福大學畢業典禮上發表演說時，他講述了他為什麼會從大學輟學。

sentences.en: It was pretty scary at the time, he said, but looking back, it was one of the best decisions I ever made.
sentences.zh: 他說，當時情況挺嚇人的，但回想起來，這是我做過最好的決定之一。

sentences.en: Dropping out allowed him to drop in on classes that interested him, rather than classes he was being told to attend.
sentences.zh: 輟學讓能夠去旁聽那些他感興趣的課程，而不是去上那些被要求去上的課。

sentences.en: He said,
sentences.zh: 他說，

sentences.en: I didn't have a dorm room, so I slept on the floor in friends' rooMs.
sentences.zh: 我沒有宿舍房間，所以我睡在朋友房間的地板上。

sentences.en: I returned Coke bottles for the five-cent deposits to buy food with,
sentences.zh: 我靠退還可口可樂瓶來賺取五分錢的押金以購買食物，

sentences.en: and I would walk the seven miles across town every Sunday night to get one good meal a week at the Hare Krishna temple.
sentences.zh: 每星期天晚上，我都會步行七英里穿過城鎮，去奎師那派神廟吃一頓每週一次的好飯。

sentences.en: I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我愛極了。

sentences.en: And much of what I stumbled into by following my curiosity and intuition turned out to be priceless later on.
sentences.zh: 而我順應好奇心與直覺偶然涉足的許多事物，後來證明都是無價之寶。

sentences.en: At Babson College, Jennifer Tostikara studies the nature and meaning of work.
sentences.zh: 在巴布森學院，珍妮佛·托斯蒂卡拉研究工作的本質與意義。

sentences.en: Jen, you say that the notion that we can find meaning and pleasure in work is relatively recent.
sentences.zh: 珍，你說過我們能在工作中找到意義與快樂的這個觀念是相對較近的事。

sentences.en: How recent?
sentences.zh: 有多近？

sentences.en: The idea of work as a calling goes way, way back to the Protestant Reformation,
sentences.zh: 將工作視為天職的想法可以追溯到很久很久以前的宗教改革時期，

sentences.en: where the idea was work could be a calling,
sentences.zh: 當時的觀點是工作可以是一種天職，

sentences.en: and specifically that calling was to the ministry, to the clergy, to serve God directly.
sentences.zh: 具體而言，這種天職是獻身於神職、牧職，直接為上帝服務。

sentences.en: Now, work as a secular calling started to gain a foothold around the time that we started having knowledge work.
sentences.zh: 如今，作為世俗天職的工作大約在我們開始擁有知識型工作時開始站穩腳跟。

sentences.en: So kind of 80s, 90s, where I have a project I can own, I can really invest myself into.
sentences.zh: 所以大約在80年代、90年代，我有一個我可以掌控的專案，我可以真正投入其中。

sentences.en: And so therefore, I really feel like it's more than just my job, it's me.
sentences.zh: 因此，我真的覺得這不僅僅是我的工作，這就是我。

sentences.en: I'm actually putting me into it.
sentences.zh: 我實際上是把自己投入其中。

sentences.en: I would say that the time of this Steve Jobs commencement speech, 2005, is right around the time of peak calling.
sentences.zh: 我想說，史蒂夫·賈伯斯這場畢業典禮演講的時期，即2005年，正是天職熱潮達到頂峰的時期。

sentences.en: And if you look at Google n-grams for find your calling or find your passion, it really follows this.
sentences.zh: 如果你查看谷歌關於「找到你的天職」或「找到你的熱情」的詞頻統計，它確實遵循了這個規律。

sentences.en: We see this, like, you know, meandering line, very low, starting to uptick in the early 1980s,
sentences.zh: 我們看到這種，你知道的，蜿蜒的線條，非常低，在20世紀80年代初開始上升，

sentences.en: and then reaching this, you know, kind of insane, asymptotic, almost peak in right around the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 然後在2000年代初左右達到這種，你知道的，有點瘋狂的、漸近線式的、幾乎是頂峰的狀態。

sentences.en: And so, you know, while this idea has deep roots, we don't assume this is a calling from a higher power,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，雖然這個想法有著深厚的根基，但我們並不認為這來自更高權力的天職，

sentences.en: but that the experience of the calling is very, very personal, very deep, and very sort of connected to this sense of self.
sentences.zh: 而是對天職的體驗是非常非常個人化的、非常深層的，並且與這種自我意識密切相關。

sentences.en: So your own research has explored the effects of having a calling.
sentences.zh: 所以你自己的研究探討了擁有天職的影響。

sentences.en: You've examined the happiness levels of people who have found a calling.
sentences.zh: 你檢視了找到天職的人的幸福感水平。

sentences.en: Are these people more engaged and satisfied with their work, Jay?
sentences.zh: 這些人對他們的工作是否更有投入感和滿足感呢，傑伊？

sentences.en: Yeah, they are.
sentences.zh: 是的，他們的確如此。

sentences.en: So I conducted, along with my co-authors, Shassa Debrau, Hannah Weissman, and Danny Heller,
sentences.zh: 所以我和我的合著者夏莎·德布勞、漢娜·威斯曼以及丹尼·海勒一起，

sentences.en: we conducted about a 20-year survey, quantitative survey, of results on what it means to experience work as a calling.
sentences.zh: 我們進行了一項大約20年的調查，量化調查，關於體驗工作作為天職意味著什麼的結果。

sentences.en: And we found very strongly that people with strong callings report greater satisfaction with their work and their life,
sentences.zh: 我們非常強烈地發現，擁有強烈天職感的人報告出對他們的工作和生活有更高的滿意度，

sentences.en: and with engagement at work, and some behavioral indicators of better performance, lower absenteeism.
sentences.zh: 對工作的投入度也更高，並且有一些表現更好、缺勤率更低的比績效指標。

sentences.en: And these are sort of consistent findings across studies about how and why experiencing work as a calling matters.
sentences.zh: 這些是跨研究的一致發現，關於如何以及為什麼將工作體驗為天職是重要的。

sentences.en: So Steve Jobs argued that having a calling allows you to work hard because you're working with passion.
sentences.zh: 所以史蒂夫·賈伯斯認為，擁有天職能讓你努力工作，因為你是帶著熱情工作的。

sentences.en: Do you find that?
sentences.zh: 你發現是這樣嗎？

sentences.en: Is that borne out by the evidence?
sentences.zh: 這得到了證據的證實嗎？

sentences.en: Are people with a calling, do they have a higher propensity for hard work?
sentences.zh: 擁有天職的人，他們努力工作的傾向是否更高？

sentences.en: In a study with Shassa Debrau and Heather Kappes, we looked at this very question of,
sentences.zh: 在一項與夏莎·德布勞和希瑟·卡普斯的合作研究中，我們探討了這個確切的問題，

sentences.en: do strong callings lead to greater effort?
sentences.zh: 強烈的天職感是否會帶來更大的努力？

sentences.en: And we found empirically that they do.
sentences.zh: 我們從經驗上發現確實如此。

sentences.en: So when you have a stronger calling, you will expend more effort on calling relevant tasks.
sentences.zh: 因此，當你有更強烈的天職感時，你就會在與天職相關的任務上花費更多的精力。

sentences.en: So not just any task, right?
sentences.zh: 所以不只是任何任務，對吧？

sentences.en: It has to be sort of, so if my calling is toward my work domain, and then I'll put in more effort at work.
sentences.zh: 它必須是這樣的，如果我的天職是朝向我的工作領域，那麼我就會在工作上付出更多的努力。

sentences.en: The mechanism through which this happens is through enjoyment of that work.
sentences.zh: 實現這一點的機制是透過對該工作的享受。

sentences.en: So stronger calling means I enjoy the work more.
sentences.zh: 所以更強烈的天職感意味著我更享受這項工作。

sentences.en: Therefore, I will work harder at it.
sentences.zh: 因此，我會更努力地工作。

sentences.en: So this is the idea that if you love what you do, then you'll never work a day in your life.
sentences.zh: 這就是那個觀點：如果你熱愛你所做的事情，那麼你一生中將不會有一天是在工作的。

sentences.en: It's that idea.
sentences.zh: 就是那個觀點。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正確。

sentences.en: So other research finds that people who have a calling are more resilient.
sentences.zh: 因此，其他研究發現，擁有天職的人更具韌性。

sentences.en: They're able to better withstand setbacks.
sentences.zh: 他們能夠更好地承受挫折。

sentences.en: Why would this be the case, Jen?
sentences.zh: 為什麼會這樣呢，珍？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 對。

sentences.en: So a calling could almost be like a deep reserve of resilience, of connection to the work.
sentences.zh: 所以天職幾乎可以像是韌性的深厚儲備，與工作的一種連結。

sentences.en: This sense that even if things are not, you know, going well in work, that somehow my connection to the work that I'm doing, my belief in my ability to do it,
sentences.zh: 這種感覺是，即使事情在工作中進展得併不，你知道的，順利，某種程度上我與我所做工作的連結，我對自己做好這項工作能力的信念，

sentences.en: can help me to overcome a setback.
sentences.zh: 能夠幫助我克服挫折。

sentences.en: You conducted a study of officers serving in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你對在美國軍隊服役的軍官進行了一項研究，

sentences.en: military and compared people who felt a calling to those who did not.
sentences.zh: 並將那些感受到天職感的人與沒有這種感覺的人進行了比較。

sentences.en: Tell me about the study and what you found.
sentences.zh: 跟我講講這項研究以及你發現了什麼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 對。

sentences.en: So this was with Marco DiRenzo and Ned Paoli.
sentences.zh: 所以這是與馬可·迪倫佐和內德·保利一起做的。

sentences.en: We conducted a survey of military officers.
sentences.zh: 我們對軍官進行了一項調查。

sentences.en: So they were mid-career sort of junior officers, but with supervisory experience.
sentences.zh: 所以他們是處於職業生涯中期的初級軍官，但具備監督經驗。

sentences.en: They had about 10 to 12 years of service on average in the military.
sentences.zh: 他們在軍隊中平均服役了大約10到12年。

sentences.en: And we specifically looked at their perception that they had hit a career plateau, which is just what it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 我們特別觀察了他們對自己遇到了職業生涯停滯期的看法，這正如聽起來的那樣。

sentences.en: So rather than this sense that I'm on the typical career upward trajectory that is desired, that I have leveled off.
sentences.zh: 因此，與其感覺我正處於所期望的典型職業上升軌跡上，不如說我已經平穩了下來。

sentences.en: Basically, this subjective sense that I'm not learning and growing and developing in my current career.
sentences.zh: 基本上，這是一種主觀感覺，即我在當前的職業生涯中沒有學習、成長和發展。

sentences.en: And we found that the stronger their callings toward the military, the less likely they were to perceive that they were at a plateaued space in their career.
sentences.zh: 我們發現，他們對軍隊的天職感越強，他們越不可能認為自己處於職業生涯的停滯期。

sentences.en: That, in turn, drove their commitment to staying in the military as an organization.
sentences.zh: 這反過來又推動了他們對留在軍隊這個組織中的承諾。

sentences.en: So Steve Jobs told us that following a calling helped him be more creative.
sentences.zh: 所以史蒂夫·賈伯斯告訴我們，追隨天職幫助他變得更有創造力。

sentences.en: Is there any evidence that that is the case more generally?
sentences.zh: 有沒有任何證據表明這種情況在更廣泛的範圍內也成立？

sentences.en: Stronger callings mean you're just more deeply connected to that domain.
sentences.zh: 更強烈的天職感意味著你與那個領域的連結更加深厚。

sentences.en: You might want to learn more about it.
sentences.zh: 你可能會想更多地了解它。

sentences.en: You might want to spend more time doing it.
sentences.zh: 你可能會想花更多時間去從事它。

sentences.en: Employees with strong callings might expend resources that other employees who don't feel as strongly just simply aren't as willing to expend.
sentences.zh: 擁有強烈天職感的員工可能會消耗其他感受沒那麼強烈的員工根本不願意消耗的資源。

sentences.en: So this notion that, like Steve Jobs, like Oprah, like everyone else we talked about, a calling might mean an engulfment or immersion in the work that leads to breakthroughs.
sentences.zh: 所以這種觀念，就像史蒂夫·賈伯斯、歐普拉以及我們談到的所有人一樣，天職可能意味著對工作的全情投入或沉浸，從而帶來突破。

sentences.en: I will say we need more research to support these conclusions.
sentences.zh: 我必須說，我們需要更多的研究來支持這些結論。

sentences.en: But the notion that experiencing a strong calling leads people to do great work or their best work is very well founded.
sentences.zh: 但體驗到強烈的天職感會引導人們做出偉大的工作或他們最好的工作的觀點是有充分依據的。

sentences.en: So in your own career, Jen, you started out as a management consultant.
sentences.zh: 所以在你自己的職業生涯中，珍，你最初是一名管理顧問。

sentences.en: What was that work like for you?
sentences.zh: 那種工作對你來說是什麼樣的？

sentences.en: Yeah,
sentences.zh: 對，

sentences.en: I so I was an undergraduate business major and getting a job as a management consultant at a big firm in New York City was like a dream because I was making more money than seemed reasonable.
sentences.zh: 我所以我是個大學商科專業的學生，在紐約市的一家大公司找到一份管理顧問的工作就像是一個夢想，因為我賺到的錢似乎多得不合理。

sentences.en: I was working with smart, very interesting people.
sentences.zh: 我和聰明、非常有趣的人一起工作。

sentences.en: Consulting work is project based, so it doesn't get boring.
sentences.zh: 諮詢工作是基所以專案為基礎的，所以不會感到無聊。

sentences.en: You're always moving around new organization, new setting, sometimes a new city.
sentences.zh: 你總是在不同的組織、不同的環境中移動，有時還是一個新的城市。

sentences.en: There was travel.
sentences.zh: 有出差。

sentences.en: I was young and unencumbered.
sentences.zh: 我很年輕而且無拘無束。

sentences.en: It was all very glamorous, getting hotel points and all these kinds of things, frequent flyer miles.
sentences.zh: 這一切都非常迷人，累積飯店點數和所有這些類型的東西，飛行常客哩程。

sentences.en: But despite all these sort of objective reasons for me to love the work, I never felt like consulting was certainly my calling or even, frankly, something I wanted to stay in.
sentences.zh: 但儘管有所有這些讓我熱愛這項工作的客觀原因，我從不覺得諮詢絕對是我的天職，甚至坦白說，也不是我想繼續留下來的東西。

sentences.en: And I also noticed this real gender gap.
sentences.zh: 而且我也注意到這種真實的性別差距。

sentences.en: And this has gotten, I think, somewhat better, probably not all the way better, but somewhat better within consulting firMs.
sentences.zh: 我想這已經有所改善，可能沒有完全改善，但在諮詢公司內部確實有所改善。

sentences.en: But it was this classic thing where you would see a lot of predominantly male partners who had, you know, families, kids at home.
sentences.zh: 但這是一個典型的情況，你會看到許多主要是男性的合夥人，他們在家裡有，你知道的，家庭、孩子。

sentences.en: But the female partners, few as they are, were primarily single, no children.
sentences.zh: 但女性合夥人，儘管人數很少，主要都是單身，沒有孩子。

sentences.en: And I'm just thinking both, is this the life that I want?
sentences.zh: 我當時就在想，這是我想要的生活嗎？

sentences.en: But also, is this the work that I can really see myself doing, traveling potentially four or five days a week?
sentences.zh: 但同時也在想，這真的是我能看到自己一直在做的工作嗎，潛在地每週出差四到五天？

sentences.en: And ultimately, I decided that it was not and that I needed to do something else.
sentences.zh: 最終，我決定這不是，我需要做點別的。

sentences.en: So you eventually left the consulting firm and you became an academic.
sentences.zh: 所以你最終離開了諮詢公司，成為了一名學者。

sentences.en: Do you feel a calling when it comes to being a teacher and a researcher, Jen?
sentences.zh: 當談到成為一名教師和研究人員時，你是否感到一種天職感，珍？

sentences.en: Yeah, I do feel a calling.
sentences.zh: 是的，我確實感到一種天職感。

sentences.en: And I feel so fortunate to be able to study these questions that I've wondered about, you know, my whole life, really.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常幸運，能夠研究這些我一輩子都在好奇的問題，真的。

sentences.en: Like, why do people spend so much time at work?
sentences.zh: 比如，為什麼人們要花這麼多時間在工作上？

sentences.en: Why does work define us to the extent that it does?
sentences.zh: 為什麼工作對我們的定義達到了這種程度？

sentences.en: When we go to parties and someone says, what do you do?
sentences.zh: 當我們去參加派對，有人問，你是做什麼的？

sentences.en: We know what that means.
sentences.zh: 我們知道那是什麼意思。

sentences.en: That means, what do you do for a living?
sentences.zh: 那意思是，你是靠什麼謀生的？

sentences.en: It doesn't mean, like, what do you do in general, right?
sentences.zh: 它不是指，比如，你平時做什麼，對吧？

sentences.en: In the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美國

sentences.en: and in the Northeast, which is where I've mostly lived, what you do is who you are.
sentences.zh: 以及美國東北部，也就是我大部分時間生活的地方，你做什麼就代表你是誰。

sentences.en: I wanted to understand always more about that.
sentences.zh: 我一直想對此有更多的了解。

sentences.en: So being able to study that and to talk to real people and find out more about how this resonates with them, I mean, that is the beSt.
sentences.zh: 所以能夠研究這個並與真實的人交談，發現更多關於這如何引起他們的共鳴，我的意思是，那是最好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 對。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 對。

sentences.en: There's no interest whatsoever to you, but their enthusiasm in some ways rubs off on you.
sentences.zh: 對你來說可能完全沒有興趣，但他們在某些方面的熱情會感染到你。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我認為這絕對沒錯。

sentences.en: I would go so far as to say it probably wouldn't be a surprise to people working in an organization to hear from each person how they feel about their work.
sentences.zh: 我甚至會說，對於在組織中工作的人來說，聽到每個人對他們工作的感受，可能不會感到驚訝。

sentences.en: I think there would be something intangible that you could sense about their engagement with the work, maybe their obsession with the work,
sentences.zh: 我認為會有一些無形的東西，你可以感受到他們對工作的投入，也許是對工作的癡迷，

sentences.en: how they feel about the work that would come through.
sentences.zh: 他們對工作的感覺會透過這種方式傳達出來。

sentences.en: It can seem like a slam dunk.
sentences.zh: 這看起來似乎十拿九穩。

sentences.en: Steve Jobs was right.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·賈伯斯是對的。

sentences.en: All of us should find and pursue our callings.
sentences.zh: 我們所有人都應該找到並追求我們的天職。

sentences.en: But human nature, as you know from listening to this show, is endlessly complicated.
sentences.zh: 但正如你從收聽這個節目中所了解的那樣，人性是無比複雜的。

sentences.en: What serves us well in one domain can be an impediment in another.
sentences.zh: 在一個領域對我們有利的東西，在另一個領域可能會成為一種阻礙。

sentences.en: When we come back, the downsides of callings.
sentences.zh: 廣告過後，我們將探討天職的負面影響。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收聽的是《隱形大腦》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·維丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 這是《隱形大腦》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·維丹塔姆。

sentences.en: As you're listening to this episode, do you feel like you're hearing a description of yourself, someone who has found what they were meant to do,
sentences.zh: 當你收聽這一集時，你是否覺得你聽到的是對你自己的描述，一個找到了他們命中注定要做的事情的人，

sentences.en: someone with a purpose and a passion that transcends them?
sentences.zh: 一個擁有超越自身的目標和熱情的人？

sentences.en: Or do you feel envy of people who have found that calling and wonder whether you'll ever find something similar?
sentences.zh: 或者你對那些找到了天職的人感到羨慕，並懷疑自己是否能找到類似的東西？

sentences.en: If you have stories or questions about having a calling that you'd be willing to share with the Hidden Brain audience,
sentences.zh: 如果你有關於擁有天職的故事或問題，願意與《隱形大腦》的聽眾分享，

sentences.en: please go to a very quiet room and record a voice memo on your phone.
sentences.zh: 請走到一個非常安靜的房間裡，在你的手機上錄一段語音備忘錄。

sentences.en: Email it to us at ideas at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 發送電子郵件至 ideas@hiddenbrain.org 與我們聯繫。

sentences.en: Use the subject line, calling.
sentences.zh: 请使用主题行：calling。

sentences.en: That email address again is ideas at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 该电子邮箱地址再次是 ideas at hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: Sigmund Freud said there are two sources of human happiness.
sentences.zh: 西格蒙德·弗洛伊德曾说，人类幸福的来源有两个。

sentences.en: There was love and there was work.
sentences.zh: 一个是爱，另一个是工作。

sentences.en: Clothes, intimate, personal ties with other people are essential to flourishing.
sentences.zh: 衣物、亲密感以及与其他人的私密联系，对蓬勃发展至关重要。

sentences.en: Friends, families, and lovers make life worth living.
sentences.zh: 朋友、家庭和爱人让生活变得值得过下去。

sentences.en: But equally, he argued, work that shows we are making a difference in the world can be a source of enduring satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 但同样地，他认为，能证明我们正在改变世界的工作，也可以成为持久满足感的来源。

sentences.en: At Babson College, Jennifer Tosti-Karis has found that this is true.
sentences.zh: 在巴布森学院，詹妮弗·托斯蒂-卡里斯发现事实的确如此。

sentences.en: Meaningful work is a source of happiness.
sentences.zh: 有意义的工作是幸福的源泉。

sentences.en: Along with a philosopher, Christopher Wong-Michelson, she's the author of the book, Is Your Work Worth It?
sentences.zh: 她与哲学家克里斯托夫·王-米歇尔森合著了一本书，书名为《你的工作值得吗？》。

sentences.en: How to Think About Meaningful Work.
sentences.zh: 《如何看待有意义的工作》。

sentences.en: Jen, the idea of having a calling is so celebrated in our culture that it might come as a surprise to many people that callings can have downsides.
sentences.zh: 珍，拥有天职（calling）这种观念在我们的文化中备受推崇，以至于天职可能带来的负面影响会让许多人感到意外。

sentences.en: But you and others have found that they can be drawbacks to pursuing a vocation.
sentences.zh: 但你和其他人发现，追求职业理想其实也存在弊端。

sentences.en: For one thing, pursuing a calling seems to distort our judgment.
sentences.zh: 首先，追求天职似乎会扭曲我们的判断力。

sentences.en: You've looked at this idea specifically in the context of musicians.
sentences.zh: 你专门在音乐家的语境下研究过这个想法。

sentences.en: What do you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I agree, first of all, that this is startling to people because we have so encoded this cultural message of do what you love.
sentences.zh: 是的，首先我同意，这让人感到震惊，因为我们已经深深地将“做你爱做的事”这种文化信息内化了。

sentences.en: The money will follow.
sentences.zh: 钱随后就会来。

sentences.en: Find your calling.
sentences.zh: 找到你的天职。

sentences.en: Love your life.
sentences.zh: 热爱你的生活。

sentences.en: These are literally book titles that seem so obvious.
sentences.zh: 这些简直就是书名，听起来是那么理所当然。

sentences.en: You know, I find my calling and the rest is gravy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我找到了我的天职，剩下的都是意外之财。

sentences.en: But the reality looks very different, and musicians are fascinating to study because this is both a quintessential arts field, right?
sentences.zh: 但现实看起来非常不同，研究音乐家非常迷人，因为这既是一个典型的艺术领域，对吧？

sentences.en: We would imagine to see a lot of callings, a lot of passion toward music.
sentences.zh: 我们会想象看到很多天职，对音乐有大量的热情。

sentences.en: It's something, you know, a lot of us do pursue in some way or another.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是我们许多人以这样或那样的方式去追求的事物。

sentences.en: But yet it's a very fraught profession because we know that not everyone will make it as a professional musician who might want to.
sentences.zh: 然而这是一个充满风险的职业，因为我们知道，并不是所有想要成为专业音乐家的人都能成功。

sentences.en: And the same way with sports, arts, lots of different fields operate like this.
sentences.zh: 体育、艺术以及许多不同的领域也都是这样运作的。

sentences.en: So I've done a series of studies, and there's a series of interesting studies that have been done by my co-author, Shassa Dubrow.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了一系列研究，我的合著者沙萨·杜布罗也做过一系列有趣的研究。

sentences.en: She is not only a professor at the London School of Economics, but she is a professional bassooniSt.
sentences.zh: 她不仅是伦敦政治经济学院的教授，还是一位职业大管演奏家。

sentences.en: So she knows this world very, very well.
sentences.zh: 所以她对这个世界非常非常了解。

sentences.en: So she has been studying musicians over a long career span, so 11 years and counting.
sentences.zh: 因此，她在漫长的职业生涯中一直在研究音乐家，时间长达11年之久，而且还在继续。

sentences.en: And she started studying them when they were in a program for talented high school students who were talented at music, and she assessed their level of calling.
sentences.zh: 她在这些人参加一个针对音乐有天赋的高中生项目时开始研究他们，并评估了他们的天职水平。

sentences.en: toward music, then saw years later, do they pursue music professionally or not?
sentences.zh: 对音乐的天职感，然后看多年后，他们是否以音乐为职业？

sentences.en: Maybe not surprisingly, the stronger the calling, the more likely people are to pursue music professionally down the road.
sentences.zh: 也许并不意外，天职感越强，人们日后以音乐为职业的可能性就越大。

sentences.en: But that one of the drivers of this is not their actual ability or talent level, as we might think, but their perception that they're talented.
sentences.zh: 但推动这一结果的驱动因素不是我们可能认为的实际能力或天赋水平，而是他们对自身天赋的感知。

sentences.en: And that actually, with strong callings, people tend to have over-inflated perception of their own ability level.
sentences.zh: 事实上，怀有强烈天职感的人，往往对自己的能力水平有着过高的评估。

sentences.en: So they think they're better than they are.
sentences.zh: 所以他们觉得自己比实际更优秀。

sentences.en: And that leads them, then, to pursue this pretty risky career path.
sentences.zh: 这反过来又导致他们去追求这条相当冒险的职业道路。

sentences.en: So that started this idea that strong callings might lead to a sort of a career tunnel vision where you truly can't imagine that you won't make it because I love it so much.
sentences.zh: 这就引发了这样一种观点：强烈的天职感可能会导致一种职业隧道视野，让你真心无法想象自己不会成功，因为我太热爱它了。

sentences.en: You know, how can I not be the one to break through when this is my passion and this is my calling?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当这是我的热情所在，也是我的天职时，我怎么可能不是那个脱颖而出的人呢？

sentences.en: What happens when people who have a calling get feedback or guidance from others that, in fact, they're not as good as they think they are?
sentences.zh: 当拥有天职的人从他人那里得到反馈或指导，指出他们其实没有自己想象的那么好时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, they do not listen to that feedback.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们不听取那些反馈。

sentences.en: So Shassa and I have studied this specifically in the context of musicians.
sentences.zh: 所以沙萨和我专门在音乐家的语境下研究了这一点。

sentences.en: And so what we found was the stronger musicians calling toward music,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，音乐家对音乐的天职感越强，

sentences.en: the less likely they were to follow the advice of their private music teacher if that music teacher discouraged them from going into music.
sentences.zh: 如果私教劝阻他们不要从事音乐，他们听从私教建议的可能性就越小。

sentences.en: They would basically say, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上会说，非常感谢。

sentences.en: I disagree.
sentences.zh: 我不同意。

sentences.en: I'm doing it anyway.
sentences.zh: 我不管怎样都要做。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: And it would be very easy to say, well, why is this a bad thing?
sentences.zh: 人们很容易会说，这有什么不好的呢？

sentences.en: Shouldn't we have a sense that we are like, I want to do this and nothing's going to stop me and no one or nothing can dissuade me?
sentences.zh: 难道我们不应该有一种感觉，就像是，我想做这件事，什么都无法阻止我，没有人或任何事能劝阻我吗？

sentences.en: In fact, a lot of these archetypal, you know, calling stories like we shared earlier, Steve Jobs, et cetera, it's about overcoming these odds, right?
sentences.zh: 事实上，正如我们之前分享的那些原型故事一样，史蒂夫·乔布斯等人，讲的就是克服这些重重困难，对吧？

sentences.en: Despite everything stacked against me, I persevered and I broke through and I made it.
sentences.zh: 尽管一切对我不利，我还是坚持了下来，突破了困境并成功了。

sentences.en: And I think that can be true to a point.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在某种程度上是对的。

sentences.en: Obviously, having some self-confidence or even maybe a little bit of an overinflated self-perception might be helpful or might be adaptive or might help with resilience.
sentences.zh: 显然，拥有一些自信，甚至可能有一点过高的自我认知，可能会有所帮助，或者可能是适应性的，或者有助于增强抗挫力。

sentences.en: But it's hard not to think that there comes a point when an inability to listen to people that have our best interests at heart who are telling us,
sentences.zh: 但人们很难不认为，当达到某个点时，无法倾听那些真心为我们着想、告诉我们的人的意见，

sentences.en: giving us real feedback that the inability to listen to this might harm us in some way.
sentences.zh: 给我们真实的反馈，而无法倾听这些意见可能会在某种程度上伤害我们。

sentences.en: There are many callings that do not involve making a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 许多天职并不涉及赚大钱。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about the arts.
sentences.zh: 我在想艺术领域。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about music.
sentences.zh: 我在想音乐领域。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about sports in many cases, perhaps not all sports, but many sports.
sentences.zh: 我在想很多情况下的体育运动，也许不是所有运动，但很多运动。

sentences.en: What do we know about the economic impacts of pursuing a call engine?
sentences.zh: 对于追求天职所产生的经济影响，我们了解多少？

sentences.en: Yeah, so you're absolutely right that the more prototypical calling-oriented professions, whether it's nonprofit work, helping work, international aid work, et cetera,
sentences.zh: 是的，你说得完全没错，那些更具典型代表性的以天职为导向的职业，无论是公益工作、助人工作、国际援助工作等等，

sentences.en: tend to not be well paid.
sentences.zh: 往往薪酬不高。

sentences.en: So already many people to pursue their callings or meaningful work in general are being asked implicitly to accept a pay cut relative to I'm going to go work for that big bank and not ask too many questions,
sentences.zh: 因此，许多人为了追求天职或一般意义上有意义的工作，已经被隐性地要求接受降薪，相比于“我要去那家大银行工作并且不问太多问题”，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Or I'm going to go work for, you know, I'm going to work in a big law firm and not ask too many questions about who my clients are, things like that.
sentences.zh: 或者“我要去工作，你知道的，我要去一家大律所工作，而且对于我的客户是谁之类的问题不问太多”。

sentences.en: So already we have some sense that we ask people in society to take their love for what they're doing or the meaning they get from the work they do and substitute it for pay.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经有一种感觉，我们要求社会中的人们拿他们对所做事情的热爱，或者从所做工作中获得的意义，来替代薪水。

sentences.en: But actually we have found this in my own research and the research of others that people with stronger callings will actually make financial sacrifices to do the work that they love doing.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我们在我自己的研究以及其他人的研究中发现，天职感更强的人实际上会为了做他们热爱的工作而做出经济牺牲。

sentences.en: So suddenly the question becomes, is this potentially overwork and that basically sets people up to be taken advantage of?
sentences.zh: 因此，问题突然变成了：这是否可能是过度劳累，从而基本上让人们容易受到利用？

sentences.en: I mean, I was just going to ask you this question, which is if someone is willing to work without really seeking or demanding pay because they're saying I'm pursuing my passion,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我正想问你这个问题，那就是如果有人因为说自己在追求热情，而愿意在不真正寻求或要求报酬的情况下工作，

sentences.en: doesn't that make them vulnerable to exploitation?
sentences.zh: 这难道不会让他们变得容易遭受剥削吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对会。

sentences.en: And so that's something that I teach my students about and that I would really caution people about because we've already said that these are the good workers and that these are people that organizations really want to attract and really want to retain.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是我向我的学生传授的知识，也是我真正要告诫人们的事情，因为我们已经说过，这些人是好员工，也是组织真正想要吸引和留住的人。

sentences.en: So then if on top of that, I really feel like, gosh, no matter what I ask you to do, I ask you to come in, you know, off hours, all times of day or night,
sentences.zh: 那么如果在此基础之上，我真的觉得，天哪，无论我要求你做什么，我让你在下班时间、在白天或晚上的任何时间来，

sentences.en: always go above and beyond.
sentences.zh: 总是超越自我、做到极致。

sentences.en: Oh, I know I can't count on my other employees, but I can really count on you.
sentences.zh: 哦，我知道我指望不上其他员工，但我真的可以指望你。

sentences.en: So, you know, at what point is it unfair?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在什么点上这就不公平了？

sentences.en: Is it exploitative?
sentences.zh: 这是否具有剥削性？

sentences.en: And is it pushing into a personal space, you know, personal life in a way that is depleting and frankly would lead to burnout?
sentences.zh: 它是否以一种令人精疲力竭、坦率地说会导致职业倦怠的方式侵入了个人空间，也就是个人生活？

sentences.en: And in fact, that is what some studies have found is that people with stronger callings, the good way to say it is they go above and beyond their ideal employees.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一些研究发现，天职感更强的人——好听的说法是他们超越了自我、是理想员工，

sentences.en: The more negative way to say it is they will sacrifice personal time even when it's not paid and they do,
sentences.zh: 更负面的说法是，即使在没有报酬的情况下，他们也会牺牲个人时间，而且他们确实会这样做，

sentences.en: they can as a result report greater physical and psychological health issues, greater fatigue, stress, burnout,
sentences.zh: 因此他们可能会报告出更多身心健康问题、更严重的疲劳、压力、职业倦怠，

sentences.en: and ultimately will leave jobs because it's simply unsustainable to keep working at this pace.
sentences.zh: 并最终选择离职，因为以这种节奏继续工作简直是不可持续的。

sentences.en: You tell the story about a man named Colin Huggins.
sentences.zh: 你讲述了一个关于一个名叫科林·哈金斯（Colin Huggins）的男人的故事。

sentences.en: What is his story and how is it germane to what we're talking about here, Jen?
sentences.zh: 他的故事是什么？珍，这与我们在这里讨论的内容有什么关系？

sentences.en: Yeah, so this is another musician's story.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是另一个音乐家的故事。

sentences.en: Colin Huggins is a busker.
sentences.zh: 科林·哈金斯是一名街头艺人。

sentences.en: So he plays his 900-pound Steinway Baby Grand piano in the middle of Washington Square Park.
sentences.zh: 他把重达900磅的施坦威三角钢琴搬到华盛顿广场公园的正中央演奏。

sentences.en: So listeners may have stumbled upon him if they've walked through Washington Square Park and heard absolutely beautiful classical music being played.
sentences.zh: 听众如果在华盛顿广场公园走过并听到绝对优美的古典音乐，可能偶遇过他。

sentences.en: He would literally lug this piano from his apartment in the East Village over to Washington Square Park and the moving blankets he would lay under the piano and invite people to lay down under the piano so they could really experience the wall of sound that he was producing.
sentences.zh: 他会 literalmente 从东村的公寓把这架钢琴拖到华盛顿广场公园，把搬家毯子铺在钢琴下面，邀请人们躺在钢琴下面，这样他们就能真正体验到他所营造出的声音之墙。

sentences.en: He was doing this by choice.
sentences.zh: 他是出于自己的选择才这么做的。

sentences.en: He used to be a professional accompanist for the Joffrey Ballet.
sentences.zh: 他曾是乔弗里芭蕾舞团的专业伴奏员。

sentences.en: He described that once he got a taste of this public performance, he was hooked.
sentences.zh: 他描述说，一旦他尝到了这种公开表演的滋味，他就迷上了。

sentences.en: So he, you know, experienced a strong passion for music, a strong passion for public performance.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他体验到了对音乐的强烈热情，对公开表演的强烈热情。

sentences.en: And it may come as no surprise, this was not a lucrative way to make a living even pre-COVID.
sentences.zh: 也许并不奇怪，甚至在新冠疫情之前，这也是一种无法赚大钱的谋生方式。

sentences.en: But the last, and this is a, so this is already representing a real sacrifice to do one's work.
sentences.zh: 但最后，这是一个，所以这已经代表了为了完成工作而做出的真正牺牲。

sentences.en: But the last that I had read about Colin Huggins, and again, he's this beloved, you know, piano man of the, of the village and of Washington Square Park.
sentences.zh: 但我所读到的关于科林·哈金斯的最新消息——再说一次，他是村里和华盛顿广场公园里备受喜爱的钢琴师，

sentences.en: This was in 2023.
sentences.zh: 这是在2023年。

sentences.en: It was reported that he was homeless, so couldn't keep paying the rent in the East Village and was in fact sleeping in the park on his piano.
sentences.zh: 据报道他无家可归，因此无法继续支付东村的房租，实际上是睡在公园自己的钢琴上。

sentences.en: So this is a terribly tragic, very poignant story of sort of ultimate sacrifice to do work that one loves, sort of with, with very little concern about even meeting basic needs.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其悲惨、非常辛酸的故事，讲述了为了做自己热爱的工作而做出的终极牺牲，几乎完全不考虑满足基本需求。

sentences.en: So many people switch jobs as new opportunities come up, and if you don't like one job, you can go to another job.
sentences.zh: 随着新机会的出现，许多人会换工作，如果你不喜欢一份工作，你可以换另一份。

sentences.en: But if you're pursuing a calling and your career doesn't work out as planned, this feels emotionally very different than someone who loses a job or gets laid off from a position.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在追求天职，而你的职业生涯没有按计划发展，这在情感上的感觉与失去工作或被解雇截然不同。

sentences.en: I mean, they're both painful.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们都很痛苦。

sentences.en: But if you feel like you're doing something you're called to do, and it's deeply meaningful to you, losing out on a career like that can be very, very difficult.
sentences.zh: 但如果你觉得你正在做一件你注定要做的事，而且这对你意义重大，失去这样一份职业可能会非常非常困难。

sentences.en: Can you talk about this idea that in some ways, one of the downsides of having a calling is what happens when it doesn't work out as a career?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这样一种观点吗：在某些方面，拥有天职的负面影响之一，就是当它未能作为职业发展顺利时会发生什么？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: So not everyone is lucky enough to find work in their calling to begin with.
sentences.zh: 首先，并不是每个人都足够幸运能找到符合自己天职的工作。

sentences.en: Similarly, not everyone is able to sustain work in the calling.
sentences.zh: 同样，也不是每个人都能维持天职方面的工作。

sentences.en: And we can imagine that could be for a lot of reasons.
sentences.zh: 我们可以想象，这可能是由于很多原因造成的。

sentences.en: People might not be able to pursue their callings.
sentences.zh: 人们可能无法追求他们的天职。

sentences.en: And research by Justin Berg and others has shown that this is a deeply psychologically aversive state filled with frustration, regret, depression,
sentences.zh: 贾斯汀·博格（Justin Berg）和其他人的研究表明，这是一种深层的心理厌恶状态，充满了沮丧、遗憾、抑郁，

sentences.en: because it's not just I need a job, any job.
sentences.zh: 因为这不仅仅是“我需要一份工作，随便什么工作”。

sentences.en: You sort of have this notion that it's really got to live up to this high sense that I have of what work should be.
sentences.zh: 你会有这样一种观念，即它必须真正符合我对工作应有状态的高标准。

sentences.en: It's worth also pointing out, Jen, that the effects of the choices we make are not experienced only by ourselves.
sentences.zh: 珍，同样值得指出的是，我们所做选择的影响并非只有我们自己承担。

sentences.en: The people around us are affected as well.
sentences.zh: 我们周围的人也会受到影响。

sentences.en: We talked earlier about how the painter Paul Gauguin left France to try his luck as an artist in Tahiti.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到过画家保罗·高更（Paul Gauguin）是如何离开法国去大溪地碰运气当艺术家的。

sentences.en: Now, he may have gone into the history books as a great artist, but talk a moment about the impact of his choices on the people around him.
sentences.zh: 现在，他可能作为伟大的艺术家载入史册，但请谈谈他的选择对周围人的影响。

sentences.en: What does that legacy look like?
sentences.zh: 这种遗产看起来是怎样的？

sentences.en: Not such a good legacy, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 遗产不太好，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: So Paul Gauguin today, in the parlance of today, should be canceled, or we believe he should be canceled, because he led a life of utter selfishness at the expense of his family.
sentences.zh: 所以保罗·高更在今天，用现在的话说，应该被取消（canceled），或者我们认为他应该被取消，因为他过着一种极度自私的生活，而代价是牺牲了他的家庭。

sentences.en: He left his family behind in France when he went to Tahiti.
sentences.zh: 他去大溪地时把家人留在了法国。

sentences.en: So first of all, he was no longer there to contribute.
sentences.zh: 首先，他不在那里做出贡献了。

sentences.en: And as we said, he was not doing so well by selling his art in Polynesia that he could send money home to them.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，他在波利尼西亚卖画的收入并不好，无法给寄钱回家给他们。

sentences.en: So another way to say this is he abandoned his family in France.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他抛弃了在法国的家人。

sentences.en: And to go one step further, by all accounts, I mean, Paul Gauguin is now a very kind of,
sentences.zh: 更进一步说，据各方报道，我的意思是保罗·高更现在非常像一个，

sentences.en: his legacy is somewhat conflicted by the fact that he pursued women that he painted and had, you know, by all accounts, affairs with them.
sentences.zh: 他的遗产由于以下事实而备受争议：他追求他所画的女性，并且据各方报道与她们有染。

sentences.en: There's a story that his favorite child died and he still did not return home.
sentences.zh: 有一个故事说，他最喜欢的孩子死了，他依然没有回家。

sentences.en: And by all accounts, it sort of led to his downfall.
sentences.zh: 据各方报道，这最终导致了他的垮台。

sentences.en: He went sort of mad and, you know, kind of consumed by his own, you know, obsession to paint.
sentences.zh: 他有点发疯了，你知道的，被自己画画的痴迷所吞噬。

sentences.en: But it was sort of this all-consuming passion or obsession.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种吞噬一切的热情或执念。

sentences.en: And he died in Polynesia without having returned home to this family that he essentially left behind.
sentences.zh: 他在波利尼西亚去世，没有回到他基本上抛弃的这个家庭。

sentences.en: Being swept up by a calling can make people obsessive and single-minded.
sentences.zh: 被天职卷入其中会让人变得痴迷且一心一意。

sentences.en: That might be good for the pursuit of passion, but it can be harmful for other dimensions of life, from your physical health to your relationships with family and friends.
sentences.zh: 这可能有利于对热情的追求，但对于生活的其他维度——从你的身体健康到与家人朋友的关系——可能会有害。

sentences.en: So often, it seems, the good and the bad go hand in hand when it comes to callings.
sentences.zh: 因此，谈到天职时，好与坏往往如影随形。

sentences.en: Yeah, I would agree with that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意这一点。

sentences.en: I think it's certainly something that people should be aware of and look out for.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实是人们应该意识到并加以防范的事情。

sentences.en: So I think just in the same way that it might be this excuse, you know, we don't have to pay you as much because you really love it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，就像这可能是一个借口一样，你知道，我们不用付给你那么多钱，因为你真的很热爱它。

sentences.en: It also might be an excuse to not engage fully in areas outside of work because I'm so consumed by work and my work is the most important thing to me.
sentences.zh: 这也可能是一个不完全参与工作以外领域的借口，因为我被工作吞噬了，我的工作对我来说是最重要的事。

sentences.en: At what point do other domains of life, whatever those are, whether they're a family who depends on you, whether they're, you know,
sentences.zh: 在什么点上，生活的其他领域——无论这些领域是什么，无论是依赖你的家庭，无论是，你知道的，

sentences.en: self-care and the cultivation of a life outside work, which has, you know, merit and benefit,
sentences.zh: 自我关怀以及培养工作之外的生活（这具有价值和益处），

sentences.en: at what point do those things suffer because of this kind of all-in sense of performing the work?
sentences.zh: 在什么点上，这些事情会因为这种全心投入工作的心态而遭受损害？

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣。

sentences.en: We've talked about how the idea of having a calling is a romantic idea, but I can't stop seeing the parallels with actual romance.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论拥有天职的理念是多么浪漫，但我无法停止看到它与真正的浪漫关系之间的相似之处。

sentences.en: So a century or two ago, everyone thought that work was just how you paid the bills.
sentences.zh: 所以在几个世纪前，每个人都认为工作只是你付账单的方式。

sentences.en: But similarly, you know, a couple centuries ago, marriage was a very prosaic institution designed primarily for raising children.
sentences.zh: 同样地，你知道，几个世纪前，婚姻是一个非常平淡的制度，主要旨在抚养孩子。

sentences.en: Today, people want romantic partners who are going to be their soulmates.
sentences.zh: 今天，人们想要的是能成为他们灵魂伴侣的浪漫伴侣。

sentences.en: Similarly, people with a calling might ignore good advice.
sentences.zh: 同样，怀有天职的人可能会忽视好的建议。

sentences.en: People in love can be blind to reason.
sentences.zh: 身陷爱河的人可能会对理智视而不见。

sentences.en: And if having a calling that doesn't work out can leave you brokenhearted, failing at love can also leave you grief-stricken.
sentences.zh: 如果拥有一个没有成功的、未竟的天职会让你心碎，那么在爱中失败同样会让你痛不欲生。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, psychologically, do you think in some ways there are the same processes that are at work here?
sentences.zh: 我在想，从心理学的角度来看，你觉得在某些方面这里也存在着相同的机制吗？

sentences.en: I think they are.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是这样的。

sentences.en: I think that is so well said.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这句话说得太好了。

sentences.en: And I think they are very similar processes.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为它们的机制非常相似。

sentences.en: I want to remind listeners who maybe haven't heard the Steve Jobs commencement speech in a while.
sentences.zh: 我想提醒一下可能有一段时间没听过史蒂夫·乔布斯毕业典礼演讲的听众们。

sentences.en: He makes this parallel.
sentences.zh: 他做出了这样一个类比。

sentences.en: He says, don't settle.
sentences.zh: 他说，不要将就。

sentences.en: Keep looking until you've found that perfect fit, that job that you love.
sentences.zh: 不断寻找，直到找到那个完美的契合点，找到你热爱的那份工作。

sentences.en: It's as important in your work life as it is with your romantic partners.
sentences.zh: 它在你的工作中和在你的浪漫伴侣中同样重要。

sentences.en: I mean, he makes this literal parallel to a romantic search and the search for the perfect job.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他把寻找浪漫伴侣和寻找完美工作做了字面上的类比。

sentences.en: And just as this is a very high bar to live up to in your romantic life, this is a very high bar for any job to live up to.
sentences.zh: 正如在浪漫生活中这是一个极高的标准一样，对任何工作来说这也是一个极高的标准。

sentences.en: And again, the research bears this out.
sentences.zh: 而且再次强调，研究证实了这一点。

sentences.en: So people with stronger callings tend to be, so again, we've talked about how they're all in on work.
sentences.zh: 所以，有强烈使命感的人往往是——所以我们之前也讨论过，他们是如何全心投入工作的。

sentences.en: They're very, you know, go above and beyond, think outside of the box.
sentences.zh: 他们非常，你知道的，精益求精，勇于创新。

sentences.en: The flip side of this is they can be extremely critical of those around them, whether it's the organization, leaders, coworkers, have a view that differs from their own.
sentences.zh: 但硬币的另一面是，他们对周围的人可能会极其挑剔，无论是对组织、领导、同事，还是对那些持有不同观点的人。

sentences.en: But in terms of actually performing the work, they can be quite tough to work with.
sentences.zh: 但就实际执行工作而言，与他们共事可能会相当艰难。

sentences.en: They can have strained work relationships.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作关系可能会很紧张。

sentences.en: They will be, you know, the first to sign up if someone needs to work extra hours, but also the first to complain if a decision is made that they don't agree with or that they,
sentences.zh: 如果有人需要加班，他们会是你知道的第一个报名的人，但如果做出的决定不符合他们的意愿，或者他们

sentences.en: because again, it runs counter to my calling.
sentences.zh: 因为这再次违背了我的使命感，他们也是第一个抱怨的人。

sentences.en: So to have this lofty ideal of what the perfect job is going to feel like is just as sort of unrealistic an assumption as thinking, when I find my perfect life partner,
sentences.zh: 因此，对完美工作的感觉抱有这种崇高的理想，其实是一种不切实际的假设，就像认为当我找到完美的生活伴侣时

sentences.en: every day will be roses and sunshine and we'll never quarrel and we'll, you know, nothing will ever feel hard again.
sentences.zh: 每天都会是鲜花和阳光，我们永远不会争吵，而且你知道的，再也不会有任何艰难的感觉。

sentences.en: These are myths.
sentences.zh: 这些都是神话。

sentences.en: You know, some time ago we had the researcher Eli Finkel from Northwestern University on Hidden Brain, and he was making a very interesting argument.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不久前我们请到了西北大学的研究员伊利·芬克尔来到《隐藏的大脑》，他提出了一个非常有趣的观点。

sentences.en: His argument was that as our expectations of our romantic partners have gone higher and higher and higher, fewer of us are actually able to meet those expectations.
sentences.zh: 他的观点是，随着我们对浪漫伴侣的期望越来越高，我们当中能够满足这些期望的人实际上越来越少了。

sentences.en: So many of us, because our expectations for marriage have now become so much higher than they were two centuries ago,
sentences.zh: 因此，由于我们对婚姻的期望现在比两个世纪前高得多，我们中的许多人

sentences.en: fewer of us are actually able to reach the level where we are satisfied or we say that we're in a happy relationship.
sentences.zh: 实际上已经无法达到那种感到满足、或者说自己处于幸福关系中的水平。

sentences.en: But for those of us who actually are able to meet that standard, who are actually able to put in the time and the effort to cultivate great relationships,
sentences.zh: 但对于我们当中那些真正能够达到这个标准、真正能够付出时间和精力去苦心经营美满关系的人来说

sentences.en: they're probably having much happier marriages than people two centuries ago.
sentences.zh: 他们的婚姻可能比两个世纪前的人要幸福得多。

sentences.en: But it also means that there are many, many people who feel like they're falling short.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也意味着，有许许多多的人觉得自己没有达到标准。

sentences.en: And again, I can't help but see the parallels here with having a calling.
sentences.zh: 而且话说回来，我不禁发现这与拥有使命感有着相似之处。

sentences.en: If you have a calling, you happen to be lucky enough to achieve that calling.
sentences.zh: 如果你有使命感，并且恰好足够幸运实现了这种使命感。

sentences.en: You're doing work that's meaningful.
sentences.zh: 你正在从事有意义的工作。

sentences.en: You're doing work that transforms the world.
sentences.zh: 你正在从事改变世界的工作。

sentences.en: I mean, you're clearly happier than almost everyone in human history who's ever had a job.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你显然比人类历史上几乎所有拥有过工作的人都要幸福。

sentences.en: But if everyone aspires to that very, very high standard, lots of us are going to be disappointed.
sentences.zh: 但如果每个人都追求那个非常非常高的标准，我们当中就会有很多人感到失望。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is a perfect parallel.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真是一个完美的类比。

sentences.en: So first, I think someone should do that study about exactly how do people feel about the expectation of the calling versus the real.
sentences.zh: 所以首先，我认为应该有人去做这样一项研究，研究人们对使命感的期望与现实究竟有何感受。

sentences.en: I want to see that, you know, that type of study.
sentences.zh: 我想看到，你知道的，那种类型的研究。

sentences.en: But I also think that's right because we know that there are so many jobs that need doing that are unlikely to feel like people's callings.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为这是对的，因为我们知道有太多需要完成的工作，它们不太可能会让人觉得是自己的使命。

sentences.en: And so where does that leave people who are left out of this ability to, you know, choose work freely,
sentences.zh: 那么，这让那些无法自由选择工作、

sentences.en: work in areas that have a reasonable enough degree of autonomy that there's something that they can tap into?
sentences.zh: 无法在拥有足够自主权、能让他们有所投入的领域工作的人情何以堪呢？

sentences.en: I think that phenomenon will absolutely play out in a very similar way.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种现象绝对会以非常相似的方式上演。

sentences.en: I have to say that I feel torn here after this conversation because I think I want to live in a world that has Marie Curie's and Steve Jobs's,
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，在这次对话之后我感到很矛盾，因为我觉得我想生活在一个有玛丽·居里和史蒂夫·乔布斯的世界里，

sentences.en: but I can also see the great costs that come from being so single-minded.
sentences.zh: 但我也能看到如此专一所带来的巨大代价。

sentences.en: After doing all this research and thinking, where do you come down, Jen, are callings a good thing?
sentences.zh: 在做了所有这些研究和思考之后，简，你的结论是什么？使命感是一件好事吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what I like to say is, absolutely, people should not be doing work that feels meaningless, that is drudgery,
sentences.zh: 所以我想说的是，绝对的，人们不应该从事那些毫无意义、枯燥乏味的工作，

sentences.en: and that you believe is not just not making the world a better place, but might actually be making the world a worse place.
sentences.zh: 并且你认为它不仅没有让世界变得更好，甚至可能让世界变得更糟。

sentences.en: That's a fate I wouldn't want for anyone, so, you know,
sentences.zh: 那是我绝不希望任何人遭遇的命运，所以，你知道的，

sentences.en: my great hope would be that we as a society figure out how to offer jobs that provide a path to a sense that the work is meaningful and worthy of respect and human dignity.
sentences.zh: 我最大的希望是我们作为一个社会，能够找出如何提供这样一些工作：它们能让人产生一种工作有意义、值得尊重并具有人类尊严的途径。

sentences.en: I do also want to say, I don't think that feeling that work is a strong calling is the only path or the best path to feeling that you have a good life or a meaningful life.
sentences.zh: 我也想说，我不认为觉得工作是一种强烈的使命感是拥有美好生活或有意义生活的唯一途径或最佳途径。

sentences.en: So there are lots of people who find the meaning in their life outside of the meaning of their work.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多人在工作意义之外的地方找到了生活的意义。

sentences.en: So in some ways, it's sort of like what you had said.
sentences.zh: 所以在某些方面，这有点像你刚才所说的。

sentences.en: If you're lucky enough to find work that you love doing, that's great.
sentences.zh: 如果你足够幸运，能找到自己热爱的工作，那当然很好。

sentences.en: But I think for those who haven't yet found it or maybe will never find it, don't despair.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对于那些还没找到、或者可能永远找不到的人来说，不要绝望。

sentences.en: That's not a personal or moral failing as we sometimes make it seem.
sentences.zh: 正如我们有时表现出来的那样，这并不是个人或道德上的失败。

sentences.en: And there are so many ways that we can feel like we're making a difference and a contribution.
sentences.zh: 而且我们有很多很多方式可以让自己觉得我们在产生影响、作出贡献。

sentences.en: It doesn't only need to be through our work or primarily through our work.
sentences.zh: 它不一定非要通过我们的工作来实现，或者主要通过我们的工作来实现。

sentences.en: And there are lots of things that give our lives meaning that have nothing to do with work.
sentences.zh: 有很多东西赋予了我们生命的意义，而这些与工作毫无关系。

sentences.en: Jennifer Tostikaris and philosopher Christopher Wong Michelson are the authors of the book, Is Your Work Worth It?
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗·托斯蒂卡里斯和哲学家克里斯托弗·王·米歇尔森是《你的工作值得吗？如何思考有意义的工作》一书的作者。

sentences.en: How to Think About Meaningful Work.
sentences.zh: 如何思考有意义的工作。

sentences.zh: 如何能从工作中获得更多的意义和满足感。

sentences.zh: 我们将探讨那些能够改变你与工作、同事以及职业之间关系的心理学技巧。

sentences.en: So, oh, we're having a good time, we're feeling jokey with each other, and something happened.

sentences.en: But maybe I can just, like, keep going with the playfulness, and it'll just wash away.
